items.summary: أصدرت محكمة التحكيم الرياضي، بيانًا مهمًا، حددت فيه موعد حسم أزمة نهائي أمم أفريقيا 2025 بين المغرب والسنغال.
items.body: أصدرت محكمة التحكيم الرياضي، بيانًا مهمًا، حددت فيه موعد حسم أزمة نهائي أمم أفريقيا 2025 بين المغرب والسنغال. وتوج المنتخب السنغالي باللقب الأفريقي، على حساب المغرب، بعد فوزه 1-0 في المباراة النهائية، بعد التمديد للوقت الإضافي. لكن الاتحاد الأفريقي لكرة القدم، أصدر قرارًا بعد ذلك، بسحب اللقب القاري من السنغال، ومنحه إلى المغرب، وذلك بعد أحداث انسحاب لاعبي أسود التيرانجا خلال اللقاء، احتجاجًا على احتساب ركلة جزاء لأسود الأطلس قبل نهاية الشوط الثاني. وعقدت جلسة الاستماع، في مقر محكمة كاس في لوزان، الخميس 8 أكتوبر/تشرين أول الجاري، خلف الأبواب المغلقة. وقالت المحكمة في بيان ، عبر موقعها الرسمي، إنه من المتوقع صدور الحكم في نهاية شهر نوفمبر/تشرين ثان المقبل. وتابع البيان "بدأت هيئة التحكيم، مداولاتها وتستمر فيها حالياً. وقد قرر محكّمو محكمة التحكيم الرياضي، إصدار قرار كامل يتضمن الأسباب والحيثيات القانونية". وشدد "ستتطلب هذه العملية عدة أسابيع، ومن المتوقع صدور حكم المحكمة في نهاية الشهر المقبل". ناقش الموضوعات والأخبار بشكل أعمق في منتديات كووورة

items.title: قبل القمة الأوروبية.. يامال ينذر سان جيرمان برسالة من 3 كلمات
items.summary: لامين سيكون تحت ضغط كبير
items.body: لامين سيكون تحت ضغط كبير وجه لامين يامال، نجم برشلونة، رسالة إلى باريس سان جيرمان، قبل مواجهة الفريقين المرتقبة غدا الثلاثاء، في دوري أبطال أوروبا. ويستضيف باريس سان جيرمان برشلونة، غدا الثلاثاء، ضمن منافسات الجولة الثالثة من مرحلة الدوري ببطولة دوري أبطال أوروبا.  وتُعدّ هذه المباراة مهمة للغاية، حيث يدرك لامين يامال، أنه سيكون تحت ضغط كبير لتقديم أداء مميز. وقدّم الجناح البالغ من العمر 19 عامًا بداية موسم استثنائية بتسجيله 9 أهداف وصناعته 10 أهداف في 11 مباراة. ناقش الموضوعات والأخبار بشكل أعمق في منتديات كووورة وصل لامين يامال، إلى العاصمة الفرنسية برفقة زملائه في نادي برشلونة، اليوم الإثنين، وهو مفعم بالثقة. وفي لحظة وثقها زميله جول كوندي على حسابه في سناب شات ، وجّه يامال رسالة إلى باريس سان جيرمان قائلاً : "باريس، أنا قادم!".

items.summary: The 34-year-old singer told fans in a Story that vaping is very hard to quit and that it's "not worth it."
items.body: Selena Gomez has always made a point of being very honest with her fans. Which is why it was not surprising that in a candid Instagram Story post on Sunday (Oct. 18), the 34-year-old singer got real about the negative effects of vaping nicotine has had on her voice. “I’m not gonna be able to change my voice,” she said in the post . “I vaped nicotine a lot … Nicotine is so hard to quit, and I think I just wanted to say, if you’re going through it, or if you’re even trying to vape, it’s just not worth it. It’s so stupid, and it’s changed my voice.” The singer said that if fans don’t like hearing her voice it’s totally fine. “Just don’t listen to it. Just don’t listen,” she suggested. The good news is that Gomez said she’s excited because she’s stopped vaping. “I just hope that I can keep it up,” she added before giving her fans a positive affirmation to hold onto. “If you are going through something, you can get through it too. items.title: Spotify is cracking down on Family plan sharing, but you can still bypass the checks
items.summary: The streaming platform is using dynamic QR codes to enforce household rules this time.
items.body: Credit: Ryan Haines / Android Authority TL;DR Spotify is cracking down on Family plan sharing by requiring members to complete dynamic QR code address scans in person. Unverified users have seven days to complete the scan or face demotion to the Free tier and a 12-month ban on joining shared Family or Duo plans. Screenshots aren’t feasible with these dynamic QR codes, so subscribers are sidestepping the check by screen-sharing across multiple devices. Spotify is stepping up enforcement of its household location rules, leaving several Premium Family plan subscribers suddenly booted off their shared plans. The streaming giant is cracking down on family plan sharing to ensure that all members reside at the same location as the plan manager. A growing number of Reddit users are reporting that Spotify Family plan account holders are receiving sudden address re-verification prompts, particularly if they are not at the same location as other users on the Family plan. This re-verification is seemingly being done in person, with constantly refreshing QR code scans between the plan manager’s device and the member’s phone to confirm they live in the same household.

The placing matches their previous best with 2011’s Idols and 2013’s Brand New Machine . With the Pixel 11 Pro , the company is taking things even further, quite literally, with 120x Pro Res zoom. That’s a step up from 100x on the Pixel 10 Pro and a ridiculous amount of magnification for a phone. Google claims its brighter telephoto camera can capture more detail from farther away – when combined with generative AI, of course. But just because a phone can zoom in that far doesn’t mean the results will be any good. My previous experience with such bold claims has often fallen flat. So, I was curious to see if Google could do any better. I spent the past week testing the Pixel 11 Pro’s zoom in different situations to see if it actually holds up or is just something that looks good on a spec sheet. items.title: I’ve been a smart home user for 10 years, and the Apple HomeView looks like a game-changer
items.summary: From intrusive ads to clunky software, the smart home landscape has a lot of room to improve. The HomeView could help.
items.body: Smart displays are a category that, to me, have always felt like they’re on the cusp of being the next big thing for the smart home. I was excited when I first got my Nest Hub . The idea that I could control connected devices with a tap, without having to shout commands at a speaker or pull out my phone, was incredibly appealing. Want to turn off the lights? Just tap a button. Simple, practical. Fast forward to today, and it’s hard not to feel like the category has gone nowhere. Google’s Nest Hub displays are getting long in the tooth, while Amazon’s Echo Show lineup has become increasingly difficult to recommend when so much of the screen real estate is effectively used as a digital billboard. For something that’s supposed to make your home more convenient, that’s a pretty disappointing state of affairs.

items.body: I got my hands on the Google Pixel 11 Pro XL when it launched globally in August, and I’ve spent quite a bit of time with it since. It’s not my daily driver, but I’ve used it enough to know what I love about it and, more importantly, where I wish Google had done things differently. If there’s one thing I’ve come to appreciate about Pixel phones over the years, it’s how Google gets so many of the little things right. From the design and software to how everything feels in everyday use, using a Pixel has a certain charm that’s hard to ignore. Of course, that doesn’t mean everything is perfect. I’m referring to smartphones that have one or two deal-breakers, in spite of their positive first impressions. It could be as trivial as a missing feature, or more unforgivable like a substantial price hike. Whichever it may be, I’d rather save my money for something else.

Even when I can’t mount my phone to my car dashboard, I use its audio navigation to guide me to destinations I’m not familiar with. But as the app has rolled out newer features, I’ve had a habit of ignoring them. My You tab remains neglected, and I’ve only ever left two reviews (both seven years ago) in the app. I also happily ignore the recommendations that appear when I’m about to search for something. However, recently I decided to revisit the lists and labeled places features — and realized that I’ve been missing out.

The changes follow an ESA complaint accusing ANBERNIC of selling devices bundled with unauthorized games. ANBERNIC hasn’t confirmed a connection, but the move may be intended to head off further action against the company. ANBERNIC has had quite a week. After recently unveiling its Nintendo 3DS-inspired RG DDS handheld — whose potential pricing was leaked earlier today — the company found itself facing scrutiny over the copyrighted games allegedly bundled with its devices. Within days of the complaint coming to light, ANBERNIC now appears to be quietly removing the contentious microSD card options from its online store. As spotted by Retro Handhelds , several ANBERNIC handheld listings have lost the option to purchase additional microSD cards alongside the devices. The publication compared an archived version of the RG SP listing from August 14 with the current storefront, finding that only the 16GB option remains. That card is still needed because it contains the handheld’s stock firmware.
